items.title: Former High Court Chief Justice among 6 candidates for SCBA President
items.summary: Senior Advocate Siddharth Mridul , who earlier served as Chief Justice of Manipur High Court filed his nomination for the post of Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) President on Thursday. Launching his campaign with the slogan, “No promises, only work,” Mridul filed his nomination ahead of the SCBA elections, which are scheduled to be held later this month under the existing electoral rules. Mridul was designated as a Senior Advocate in 2006 and also served as Standing Counsel and Senior Panel Counsel for the Union government. Earlier in his career, he was elected twice to the Bar Council of Delhi, where he served as Honorary Secretary and later as Vice-Chairman. He was later appointed as judge of the Delhi high Court and went on to serve as the Chief Justice of Manipur High Court. After retirement as a judge, he returned to law practice. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court appointed him to chair a High-Powered Election Committee overseeing elections to certain State Bar Councils. Apart from Mridul, several other prominent members of the Bar have also filed their nominations for the post of SCBA President. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday directed the Rajasthan government to constitute an Integrated Coordination Group to coordinate efforts to tackle industrial pollution and restore polluted river systems in the State [ In Re: 2 Million Lives At Risk, Contamination In Jojari River, Rajasthan ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the order while dealing with a suo motu case concerning the industrial pollution of rivers in Rajasthan, including the Jojari River. The Court ordered the coordination group's constitution after noting that the environmental issues before it could not be effectively addressed through fragmented departmental interventions. The Court added that the coordination group will be headed by Rajasthan Chief Secretary Voruganti Srinivas and may include senior officials from various government departments, the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board (RSPCB), other statutory authorities and experts. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale nevertheless took into account a medical report submitted by the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) which said that while Asaram might not require hospitalisation, he might need round-the-clock medical assistance. Hence, the Court ordered that Asaram will be at liberty to avail the assistance of a trained care taker of his choice on round-the-clock basis. "We have taken note of the letter dated July 31, 2026 by the AIIMS. items.title: NLSIR reveals theme for inaugural Chief Justice ES Venkataramiah Memorial Best Essay Prize
items.summary: National Law School of India Review (NLSIR) has announced the theme for the inaugural edition of the Chief Justice ES Venkataramiah Memorial Best Essay Prize. The theme for this inaugural edition has now been announced as Does the Constitution Choose an Economic Model? Directive Principles and the Question of Ideological Neutrality. The theme draws on the Supreme Court's 2024 nine-judge Bench ruling in Property Owners' Association v. State of Maharashtra . The Bench had considered whether all privately owned property falls within the expression "material resources of the community" under Article 39(b) of the Constitution, a Directive Principle that asks the State to distribute the community's resources for the common good. The majority, led by then Chief Justice DY Chandrachud , held that it does not, reasoning that the Constitution does not commit India to a single economic ideology, and that treating all private property as a material resource would require the Court to endorse one particular vision of the country's economic and social order. items.summary: The Union Government has opposed a plea seeking income-based prioritisation within reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SC/STs), Other Backward Classes (OBC) and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). In an affidavit filed before the top court, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment also said that the creamy layer principle cannot be applied to SC/STs and that only parliament can alter the lists of communities classified as SC/STs. Hence, the plea is misconceived and ought to be dismissed with exemplary costs, it was submitted. On the issue of whether the creamy layer concept, used to exclude the financially well placed among OBCs, could be extended to SC/STs as well, the government relied on the nine judge bench ruling in Indra Sawhney case to reject the suggestion. It was pointed out that the discussion on excluding the socially advanced in that judgment was expressly "confined to OBCs only and has no relevance in the case of SC/STs." The government further submitted that a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in Ashoka Kumar Thakur judgment had clarified that for the purpose of reservation, the principles of creamy layer are not applicable to SC/ STs. items.summary: The protest by state service aspirants in Jharkhand, alleging irregularities in recruitment examinations, is growing by the day. Launched on July 25 from Ranchi’s Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium under the banner of the ‘JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch’, the protest entered its 14th day on Friday. Meanwhile, political pressure on the Hemant Soren government continues to mount. The immediate trigger for the protest were the results of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Civil Services Preliminary Examination released on July 5. Protesters have alleged large-scale irregularities in the examination and selection process. They are demanding the cancellation of the exam and calling for a probe by the CBI or the formation of a committee comprising retired High Court judges from outside Jharkhand to investigate the matter. Since its inception, however, the movement has expanded beyond grievances related to a single exam’s results to demand comprehensive and structural reforms within the JPSC and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).
